column3: The Hebrew first says Jerubbaal rose early and refers to the Midianite camp as north of singular “him”; BSB combines the early rising with camping and uses plural “them.”
The Hebrew has singular “their hand”; BSB has plural “their hands.”
The Hebrew explicitly says to proclaim “in the ears” of the people; BSB says “in the hearing.”
The Hebrew repeats “with you” in both the instruction and confirmation about the man who goes; BSB omits it in the confirmation “he shall go.”
The Hebrew leaves Gideon unnamed at the start and explicitly names him in the divine speech introduction; BSB names him at the start and uses “him” in the introduction.
The Hebrew uses singular collective “their hand” and “their mouth” and explicitly says they knelt “on their knees”; BSB has plural “hands” and “mouths” and simply “knelt.”
The Hebrew says each person should go “to his place”; BSB says to “go home.”
The Hebrew begins with taking the provisions and horns and then dismissing Israel’s men; BSB places the dismissal first and makes the taking a relative clause about the three hundred.
The Hebrew says the LORD spoke “to him”; BSB explicitly names Gideon.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says the hands will grow strong and then to go down into the camp; BSB uses the passive “will be strengthened” and an explicit purpose “to attack the camp.”
The Hebrew calls the eastern people “sons of the east”; BSB says “all the other people of the east,” supplying “other.”
The Hebrew repeats the dream root and twice states falling, including an active overturning action; BSB has a single “dream” in the quotation and says the tent “overturned and collapsed.”
The Hebrew has both “answered” and “said”; BSB gives a single “replied.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the companies “heads” and explicitly says the jars were empty; BSB has “companies” and “large jar,” supplying “large” and omitting “empty.”
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed and repeats “so you shall do”; BSB names Gideon and uses “exactly” for the second command.
The Hebrew begins with singular “I will blow the horn”; BSB has plural “I and all ... blow our horns.”
The Hebrew says they had just raised or posted the guards; BSB describes “the changing of the guard.”
The Hebrew explicitly states the horns were held “to blow”; BSB leaves that purpose implicit in the description of holding them.

The Hebrew does not explicitly name Israelites or Midianites in this verse and separately states running, shouting, and fleeing; BSB supplies those identities and combines the enemy’s actions as fleeing while crying out and running.
The Hebrew makes each man’s sword the object God turns against his neighbor; BSB makes the men the object and says “with their swords.”
The Hebrew uses singular collective “man of Israel” and names Midian; BSB has plural “men” and “Midianites.”
The Hebrew twice names “the waters ... and the Jordan”; BSB combines them as “the waters of the Jordan.”
The Hebrew repeats the killing verb for Oreb and Zeeb and uses singular collective “head”; BSB gives the killing once for both and uses plural “heads.”
